column5: ConvexHull: lexicographic (x,z) strict weak order over finite points (Update drops non-finite); elements that compare equal are bit-identical points and std::unique follows, so any sort gives the same sequence. slam_refact extension ACC-3 (no original counterpart)
Median(): only v[m] is read, and the m-th order statistic of finite floats does not depend on the algorithm (equal values are numerically equal; only a -0.0/+0.0 sign could differ). ACC-3 extension
pairs (frame,id) with unique ids: a total order, so the sorted sequence and the dropped oldest points are identical on every library. ACC-3 extension

candidates ordered by height. Candidates with equal height are identical surfaces (inliers, hull and area are functions of the height only), so tie order cannot change the merged list. ACC-3 extension
state_.others ordered by inliers desc, then height asc: a total order (merged heights are >= 3 bins apart, hence distinct), so the sequence is identical on every library. ACC-3 extension
hits ordered by distance, then HitType, then surface: a total order ((type, surface) is unique per hit), so exact distance ties no longer depend on the library. ACC-3 extension
gravity_angle_deg(): only a[size/2] (the median of doubles) is read; the order statistic is algorithm-independent. ACC-5 extension, off by default
sorts directory names of recorded sets (unique within one directory, total order on strings); gate tooling, not engine output
sorts file names of one directory (unique, total order on strings); gate tooling, not engine output
SetHash sorts 48-byte records with operator< (total order on bytes) before hashing; equal records are byte-identical
